Visible machining marks, light surface scratches. Anodizing Anodizing creates a corrosion-resistant, uniform, matte or glossy finish. Parts can be anodized in different colors—black, red, and gold are most common. Hardcoat Anodizing A type of anodizing that produces a thicker and harder coating on the surface, resulting in increased wear resistance and durability. Conductive Anodizing An anodizing process that creates a conductive oxide layer on the surface, typically used for EMl/RFl shielding or electrical grounding applications. Powder Coating Electrostatic dry powder application cured under heat. Eco-friendly, durable finish with superior corrosion resistance for metal parts. Brushing Parts are brushed using an abrasive tool to create a pattern of fine parallel lines on the material surface, producing a unique aesthetic effect. Silkscreen A part marking technique that uses a fine mesh screen to apply ink onto a surface, to print the desired text or image onto the substrate. Laser Marking Laser marking uses a laser beam to create permanent marks or designs on the surface of a material, typically resulting in high precision and resolution. FAQs About Sheet Metal Manufacturing Q: Does JLCCNC offer surface finishing services for custom sheet metal parts? Yes, we provide anodizing, powder coating, laser marking, and other surface finishes, so your sheet metal parts are both durable and visually professional. Q: What’s the minimum width at the center of the bent U-shaped structure? The minimum center width required for U-shaped bends is specified by material thickness: - 1 mm thickness: minimum center width 12 mm - 2 mm thickness: minimum center width 12 mm - 3 mm thickness: minimum center width 18 mm - 4 mm thickness: minimum center width 20 mm - 5 mm thickness: minimum center width 23 mm - 6 mm thickness: minimum center width 25 mm Q: What’s the minimum cutting hole diameter for sheet metal parts? The minimum diameter of a cutting hole must be at least half the sheet thickness, and not less than 1 mm. Q: What is the minimum edge width for each material thickness, and do single and secondary bends have different length requirements? Minimum edge width varies by material thickness; single and secondary bends have distinct required lengths. Refer to the detailed length specifications Q: What are the 2D file requirements for laser marking and silkscreen printing? Requirements as follows: -Please upload the marking/silkscreen drawing based on the actual flat shape after bending (how the part looks once fully bent and flattened). Do NOT upload the unbent, unfolded sheet exported from CAD. -Clearly draw part outline and hole positions (if included). -Text (if included) must use a double-line font with a 0.2mm line width.
